design_reference: Editeur Livre-Jeu - Wireframes.dc.html § 04 « Détail de chaque écran d'action » → 4B « DÉCOR · PRENDRE » (Prendre / Écouter / Fouiller switch + object rows) and the shared object editor anatomy (NOM — interne / DESCRIPTION — lue par le joueur) reused across § 04 (PNJ donne, décor prendre, monstre loot). Mounted via node-editor's « Action requise » seam. Low-fi wireframe, light theme.

plan.goal: Let an author configure a node's « Décor » action — choose the interaction (prendre / écouter / fouiller) and, for « prendre », author a takeable object with an internal name + a player-facing description — mounted into node-editor through the ActionRegistry without coupling the two features.
acceptance_criteria: action-decor self-registers a « Décor » editor with the brain ActionRegistry; node-editor's « Action requise » control offers « Décor » with zero changes to node-editor (Open/Closed, KR-051).
Selecting « Décor » on a node mounts the décor editor body for that node; structural screens (sommaire/mort) never show it.
The décor editor offers a Prendre / Écouter / Fouiller interaction switch, persisted on the node via BookService (single source of truth).

« Prendre » shows the shared brain ObjectEditor capturing the object's internal NAME and player-facing DESCRIPTION (KR-052); the object carries a stable id minted once and preserved across edits (KR-003).
All décor config is persisted through BookService.updateNode (no private copy, KR-020) and reflects live; it lives on the node document, not in feature-local state.
node-editor never imports action-decor and vice versa; the wiring is the composition root calling registerActionDecor with the brain ActionRegistry.
The editor renders strictly from design-system primitives/tokens (SegmentedControl, ObjectEditor/Field), light theme; controls are keyboard-operable with ≥44px targets.
plan.walking_skeleton: registerActionDecor registers an ActionEditor { type:'decor', label:'Décor', render } with the brain ActionRegistry (wired at the App composition root). DecorEditor reads the node's decor config live via useOpenBook and writes it through BookService.updateNode: a Prendre/Écouter/Fouiller SegmentedControl, and for « prendre » the shared brain ObjectEditor (name + description) with a stable object id. Écouter/Fouiller are placeholder stubs for later iterations.

iterations.goal: « Prendre » full (§ 4B): multiple takeable objects as rows (useful / leurre badges), add/remove/reorder, per-object « jet requis » (caractéristique + difficulté + échec text); object edit modal.
« Écouter » / « Fouiller »: the heard/found reveal text + optional skill roll gating; surface réussite/échec outcomes (the only semantic colors).
Promote objects to a shared ObjectCatalogService (reuse « prendre dans la liste », by stable id) so décor/PNJ/monster share one object catalog and hidden-prereqs (KR-062) can reference them.

known_risks: KR-050/051 — node-editor is a host: action-decor self-registers via the ActionRegistry and is mounted by node-editor without being imported; adding the action needs zero node-editor changes.
KR-052 — objects carry a player-facing DESCRIPTION, not just a name; captured via the shared brain ObjectEditor, never a bare string.
KR-020 — décor config is read/written through BookService (the SSOT); the editor holds no private copy and reflects live via useOpenBook.
KR-003 — the takeable object is referenced by a stable id minted once (createId) and preserved across edits, never keyed by name.

KR-090 — décor config lives on the node document (node.decor); structural screens never carry it. Reuse-by-id (iter 3) is a DERIVED REFERENCE (TakeableObject own { object } | ref { objectRef }), not an owned ObjectCatalogService: a ref resolves live via collectObjects/findObject (dangling ⚠, KR-021), collectObjects skips refs (no phantom entry / no desync, KR-020), and « Prendre dans la liste » adds a ref the décor editor shows read-only (KR-062).
KR-013 — derive the editor's current values inline from the live node, not via a useEffect-synced mirror.

iterations_log.label: walking-skeleton
architecture_choices: action-decor self-registers an ActionEditor with the brain ActionRegistry at the App composition root (registerActionDecor), proving the Open/Closed seam end-to-end with the first real action feature (KR-050/051) — node-editor mounts « Décor » without importing it.

The shared ObjectEditor lives in brain/components (KR-052/109): décor « prendre » is its first consumer; PNJ/monster will reuse it without a cross-feature import. It is controlled — the owner persists onChange through BookService.
DecorEditor is a VIEW over BookService (KR-020): reads node.decor via useOpenBook, writes via updateNode; the takeable object gets a stable id minted lazily with createId (KR-003).
The domain model gained node.decor (DecorConfig) + GameObject; NodePatch carries decor so updateNode's existing text-only guard keeps it off structural screens (KR-055).
deviations_from_plan: « Écouter » / « Fouiller » are placeholder stubs (iteration 2); « prendre » ships a single object (the multi-object list + rolls are iteration 1).
Objects are embedded on the node for the skeleton; promotion to a shared ObjectCatalogService is iteration 3 (needed for hidden-prereqs, KR-062).

test_coverage.unit: ObjectEditor captures name + description (KR-052); registerActionDecor adds/removes the 'decor' editor (KR-051)
test_coverage.integration: action-decor via App — « Décor » offered through the registry seam, « prendre » edits an object persisted via BookService with a stable id, interaction switch persists + toggles the object editor

iterations_log.label: iteration-1
architecture_choices: « Prendre » became a LIST of takeable objects: the domain model gained TakeableObject (object + kind + optional roll), SkillRoll (trait/difficulty/failureText), and TakeableKind ('utile'|'leurre'); DecorConfig.objects holds the list. The walking-skeleton single DecorConfig.object is migrated to objects on read via a pure takeablesOf helper and canonicalised (legacy field dropped) on the first write (KR-090/116 spirit: a persisted book may still carry the old shape — never lose it).

utile/leurre is a closed set in a feature-local Record TAKEABLE_KINDS (KR-117): label + Badge tone written once, option list + row badge derived from it, no kind === 'utile' branch. Tones stay neutral/muted — never good/bad, reserved for réussite/échec (KR-091).

Each object is edited in an ObjectEditModal with REAL commit/cancel semantics: a local DRAFT (legitimate editing state, not a useEffect mirror — KR-013) initialised once from the takeable, keyed by object id so each open is fresh (KR-053); « Enregistrer » commits through the owner (BookService.updateNode), « Annuler »/Esc discards so a cancelled new object never lands. The modal composes the shared brain ObjectEditor (KR-052) + a kind SegmentedControl + a « jet requis » Toggle revealing caractéristique/difficulté/texte-d'échec Fields.

DecorEditor stays a VIEW over BookService (KR-020): list add/remove/reorder all write the canonical { interaction, objects } through updateNode; object ids are stable (KR-003); the row shows the name + utile/leurre Badge + a « jet » marker.

Pre-commit tech-lead review (review the uncommitted diff, fix before commit): the row ↑↓✕ actions were bumped to HIT_TARGET_MIN (44px) to meet the ≥44px AC rather than leave the choice-linking 24px precedent unmet, and the unnamed-object fallback unified to one UNNAMED constant. (The pre-existing 24px row actions in choice-linking are a separate, noted backfill — not changed in this slice.)
deviations_from_plan: « jet requis » captures the échec branch only (caractéristique + difficulté + texte d'échec) — a réussite simply takes the object — rather than the full réussite/échec OutcomesEditor; the caractéristique is author free text (a shared caractéristique catalog would be extracted at the second consumer, e.g. action-trap, like ObjectEditor/OutcomesEditor).
Écouter / Fouiller stay stubs (iteration 2); promotion to a shared ObjectCatalogService is iteration 3.

test_coverage.unit: takeablesOf migration (objects list / legacy single object / both / none), blankTakeable fresh id, TAKEABLE_KINDS non-semantic tones
test_coverage.integration: action-decor via App — add object (modal, stable id), cancel discards, multiple rows, leurre badge, remove, reorder (move up), jet requis persists trait/difficulty/failure, interaction switch hides the list

iterations_log.label: iteration-2
architecture_choices: « Écouter » / « Fouiller » gained a reveal: the domain model added DecorReveal { text, roll?, outcomes? } on DecorConfig.reveal. A new RevealEditor renders the heard/found text Field + a « jet requis » Toggle that, when on, reveals the SHARED brain controls — CHARACTERISTIQUE SegmentedControl (from CHARACTERISTICS, KR-117) + DIFFICULTÉ Stepper + the shared OutcomesEditor (réussite/échec reveal, KR-091/117) — exactly the trap roll pattern, reused not re-built (KR-109). Toggling the gate off drops roll + outcomes but keeps the base text.

écouter and fouiller share one reveal field (only one interaction is active per node); their field copy (« Ce que le joueur entend / trouve » + placeholder) lives in the DECOR_INTERACTIONS Record (KR-117), extended from { label } to also carry revealLabel/revealPlaceholder — one source, no per-interaction branch.

All décor writes were unified into a single writeDecor(patch: Partial<DecorConfig>) that re-emits the canonical { interaction, objects, reveal } (legacy `object` dropped, KR-090): editing one facet (interaction / objects / reveal) never drops the others. RevealEditor is controlled — DecorEditor persists every change via BookService.updateNode (KR-020); the editor holds no private copy (KR-013).
deviations_from_plan: One shared reveal for both écouter and fouiller (not a per-interaction reveal): a node has a single active interaction, so a second reveal field would be dead state. If an author needs distinct heard/found text they re-author after switching — acceptable for the low-fi slice.

The reveal gates on a roll with réussite/échec OutcomesEditor (the spec's « surface réussite/échec »); the prendre « jet requis » keeps its échec-only SkillRoll.failureText shape (a réussite simply takes the object) — the two roll shapes coexist as designed.

test_coverage.unit: covered via integration (RevealEditor is presentational over brain controls)
test_coverage.integration: action-decor via App — Écouter authors a reveal text + gates it (trait + stepped difficulty + réussite/échec persisted on reveal); Fouiller uses its own field copy and toggling the roll off drops roll+outcomes but keeps the text (outcome fields removed)

iterations_log.label: iteration-3 (reuse « prendre dans la liste » by id)
architecture_choices: Reuse-by-id landed as a DERIVED REFERENCE, not an owned ObjectCatalogService (user decision, the same call as the choice-linking hidden-prereq catalog, KR-062): a TakeableObject is EITHER « own » ({ object }) OR « ref » ({ objectRef }); `object` became OPTIONAL on the type with exactly one of object/objectRef set. New takeables.ts helpers takeableId / isRefTakeable / resolveTakeableObject(book, t) (own → inline object; ref → findObject(book, objectRef), null = dangling) keep every caller off the optional field.

« Prendre dans la liste » is a new ReuseObjectPicker (searchable popover, mirrors the relink picker): it lists collectObjects(book) minus the ids already present here, and adds a ref takeable. A ref is resolved LIVE so the object stays single-sourced on its authoring node (no copy, no desync, KR-020); collectObjects SKIPS refs so a reused object is never a phantom second catalog entry.

A ref row is READ-ONLY in the décor editor (the object is authored on its origin node) — it shows the resolved name + a « réutilisé » badge, or « ⚠ objet supprimé » when the reference dangles (KR-021); the ObjectEditModal only ever edits an « own » takeable. ReuseObjectPicker extracted so DecorEditor stays under the 400-line split signal (KR-112).

The hidden-prereq half of the iter-3 goal (« hidden-prereqs can reference them ») was already delivered by choice-linking iter 3 over the same derived collectObjects catalog — this slice adds the décor authoring side (reuse) on the same foundation.
deviations_from_plan: No owned ObjectCatalogService and no migration of pnj.gift / monster.loot: objects stay node-owned and the « catalog » is the derived collectObjects union. A ref's caveat — deleting the OWNER node dangles the reference (surfaced ⚠) — is the accepted trade for avoiding a second source of truth; an owned catalog could replace collectObjects transparently later since everything references by id.
A ref takeable carries its own kind (default « utile ») but is not inline-editable here (kind/roll of a reused object are deferred polish) — remove + re-add, or edit the object on its origin node.

test_coverage.unit: takeables — refTakeable/isRefTakeable/takeableId/resolveTakeableObject (own vs ref, dangling null); collectObjects ignores a ref (no phantom entry)
test_coverage.integration: action-decor via App — « Prendre dans la liste » reuses an object by id (persists objectRef, not a copy; row shows « réutilisé »); a ref to a deleted object shows « ⚠ objet supprimé »

iterations_log.label: iteration-4 (XP attribué)
architecture_choices: Added xp?: number (0–5) to DecorConfig (brain/types.ts). The Stepper is placed after the prendre/écouter/fouiller content area and before the ObjectEditModal. writeDecor canonicalisation includes xp: decor.xp so the field is preserved when interaction or objects change.

test_coverage.unit: decor.test.tsx: XP stepper increments → decor.xp === 1; decrement → 0 (floor, not negative)

open_questions: A ref takeable's own kind (utile/leurre) + jet are not inline-editable yet — a small polish if authors need to reclassify a reused object without removing it.

If an owned ObjectCatalogService is ever needed (e.g. play-mode inventory independent of any node), collectObjects can be swapped for catalog.list() transparently since décor/pnj/monster + hidden-prereqs already reference objects by stable id.
